title: How Does Marys Response To The Angels Message Serve As A Model For Believers Today
paragraphs: Mary’s Response to the Angel: A Model of Faithful Submission

The encounter between Mary and the angel Gabriel in Luke 1:26-38 ASV is one of the most profound moments in the New Testament. Mary’s response to God’s message offers timeless lessons for all who seek to follow Christ. In this study, we will explore how her reaction serves as a model for believers today, focusing on key aspects such as faith, humility, submission, and trust in God’s promises.
1. Faith in God’s Word
When Gabriel appears to Mary and tells her she will conceive the Messiah, her initial reaction is one of confusion and wonder. Yet even in the face of the impossible, Mary demonstrates faith:
And Mary said unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? - Luke 1:34 ASV

Mary’s question is not one of doubt, but of honest inquiry. She does not reject the message but seeks understanding. Her faith is evident when she accepts Gabriel’s explanation that “with God nothing shall be impossible” (Luke 1:37 ASV). Believers are called to trust God’s Word, even when circumstances seem insurmountable.
2. Humble Submission to God’s Will
Mary’s response exemplifies humility and submission:
And Mary said, Behold, the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her. - Luke 1:38 ASV

She identifies herself as the “handmaid” (servant) of the Lord, indicating her willingness to serve God’s purposes above her own. This attitude reflects the biblical principle of yielding to God’s sovereign will, as seen in Jesus’ own submission in Gethsemane (Luke 22:42 ASV).
3. Trust in God’s Promises
Mary’s confidence rests in the character and promises of God. Gabriel assures her:
For no word from God shall be void of power. - Luke 1:37 ASV

Mary’s trust is not grounded in her own ability, but in God’s faithfulness. This trust is echoed by all believers who, through faith in Christ, rely on God’s promises for salvation and daily living (2 Corinthians 1:20 ASV).
4. Willingness to Face Risk and Discomfort

Accepting God’s call meant that Mary would face misunderstanding, potential shame, and risk in her community. Yet, she embraces God’s plan despite the cost. Jesus later teaches that following Him involves taking up one’s cross and prioritizing His will above all else (Luke 9:23 ASV).
5. Rejoicing in God’s Work

After Gabriel’s visit, Mary visits Elizabeth and expresses her praise in the Magnificat (Luke 1:46-55 ASV). She rejoices in God’s salvation and His faithfulness to His people. This joyful praise is a fitting response for all who experience God’s grace through Jesus Christ (Ephesians 2:8 ASV).
Conclusion: Lessons for Believers
Mary’s response to the angel’s message stands as a model for every Christian. She responded with faith, humility, submission, trust, courage, and praise. Her example challenges believers to:
Trust God’s Word, even when it defies human understanding
Submit humbly to God’s will, regardless of personal cost
Rely entirely on God’s promises and power
Rejoice in God’s redemptive work in Christ
May we, like Mary, be willing to say, “Be it unto me according to thy word,” as we follow Jesus Christ by faith.
